scholarships.title: India Science and Research Fellowship (ISRF) Programme
scholarships.official_source: Indian National Science Academy (INSA) for Department of Science & Technology (DST), Govt. of India

existing.description: Science Academies Summer Research Fellowship Program for Students and Teachers — 2026
eligibility: Citizen or permanent resident of Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Maldives, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka or Thailand
Actively engaged in research at a university or research institution in their own country in science and technology including engineering and medical sciences
Minimum qualification: PhD / M.Tech / M.Sc / MBBS with 3-5 years research or teaching experience
Applicants registered for a PhD degree in their home country may also apply
Below 45 years of age as on 31 March 2026 (stated for the 2025-26 cycle)
May avail the fellowship only once in a five-year period
Must not hold any visa for temporary or permanent residency in India
existing.eligibility_summary: Citizens or permanent residents of Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Maldives, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka or Thailand, actively engaged in research at a university or research institution in their own country, holding PhD/M.Tech/M.Sc/MBBS with 3-5 years of research or teaching experience, below 45 years of age on the relevant cut-off date, with a valid passport and no Indian temporary or permanent residency visa.
benefits: Rs. 50,000 per month fellowship allowance including accommodation and medical facilities as available to the host institute
Rs. 10,000 one-time contingency grant to the fellow
Rs. 20,000 one-time contingency research grant to the host scientist through the institution
Local transport between airport and host institute
coverage: Monthly fellowship allowance of Rs. 50,000 which includes accommodation and medical facilities as available to the host institute
One-time contingency grant of Rs. 10,000 to the fellow
One-time contingency research grant of Rs. 20,000 to the host scientist through the host institution
Round-trip economy air fare from the applicant's country of employment to the Indian host institute
Local road or rail transport between the nearest airport and the host institute
requirements: Apply using the prescribed ISRF application format downloadable from www.dst.gov.in or www.insaindia.res.in
Applications must be duly endorsed by the Head of the home institution
Submit to the implementing agency in the partner country where one exists, otherwise to INSA New Delhi, with a copy to DST/INSA
Where hard copy or scan copy is submitted to INSA, include all supporting documents
documents: Brief write-up describing the proposed research work
Copy of degree certificate for highest qualification
Reprints of two recent publications in refereed journals
Copy of valid passport showing number, photograph, date of birth, date of issue, date of expiry and residential address
No Objection Certificate from the home institution on institute letterhead
Letter of Acceptance from the Indian host supervisor on the institute's letterhead
existing.english_requirement: Applications, the brochure and the application form are published in English by INSA.
application_method: Apply on the prescribed ISRF form downloaded from the INSA or DST website
Route through the implementing agency in the applicant country if available
Otherwise submit hard copy or scan copy with enclosures to INSA, New Delhi, endorsed by the home institution head
existing.selection_notes: Applications are considered once a year by a Selection Committee. Up to 80 fellowships are awarded annually, with 10 per country. INSA can assist in identifying an Indian host institution where necessary.
existing.best_fit: Established researchers from the eight eligible South and Southeast Asian countries with a permanent research position who want a 3-6 month research visit to an Indian host institute.
existing.notes: This is a research-visit fellowship, not a taught degree programme, so no tuition is charged or covered. INSA publishes and administers the call on behalf of the DST funding agency.
existing.application_period: Annual; applications received once a year by a Selection Committee. 2025-26 window: 31 December 2025 to 31 March 2026.
existing.deadline_display: For the 2025-26 cycle the call opened on 31 December 2025 and the official announcement states "Last date of proposal submission is 31 March 2026". That cycle has closed; the next annual call is expected to open around 31 December 2026 but no date is published yet.
existing.program_type: Visiting research fellowship (not a degree-awarding programme)

scholarships.title: UGC Junior Research Fellowship (JRF) and Research Associateship (RA) for Foreign Nationals
scholarships.official_source: University Grants Commission (UGC), Govt. of India

existing.description: Statutory body of the Government of India for coordination, determination and maintenance of standards of higher education.
eligibility: Students and teachers from developing countries of Asia, Africa and Latin America
JRF: 35 years for male candidates and 40 years for female candidates as on 1 July of the year of application
JRF: at least a high-class master's degree with a second-class bachelor's degree, or a second-class master's degree with a first-class bachelor's degree
RA: 40 years for male applicants and 45 years for female applicants as on 1 July of the year of application
RA: doctorate degree with published research work and evidence of independent research work
Application must be endorsed by the applicant's Indian embassy or mission
Foreign students already in India may apply through the university they propose to work with
existing.eligibility_summary: Students and teachers from developing countries of Asia, Africa and Latin America. JRF applicants must be 35 (male) or 40 (female) years of age as on 1 July of the year of application and hold at least a high-class master's degree with a second-class bachelor's degree, or a second-class master's degree with a first-class bachelor's degree. RA applicants must be 40 (male) or 45 (female) and hold a doctorate with published and independent research work.
benefits: Monthly JRF fellowship for four years
Monthly RA fellowship fixed for four years
Annual contingency grant for both JRF and RA
Departmental assistance to the host institution
Hostel accommodation or house rent allowance per host institution rules
Leave of up to 30 days a year in addition to public holidays
coverage: JRF monthly fellowship of Rs. 12,000 for the initial two years and Rs. 14,000 for the remaining period
JRF contingency of Rs. 12,000 per annum for Science or Rs. 10,000 per annum for Humanities and Social Sciences, rising to Rs. 25,000 or Rs. 20,500 per annum for the remaining period
Departmental assistance of Rs. 3,000 per annum per JRF
Escort or handicapped allowance of Rs. 2,000 per annum per JRF
RA monthly fellowship of Rs. 16,000 fixed for four years
RA contingency of Rs. 30,000 per annum
Departmental assistance of 10% of the associateship to the host institution
House rent allowance as per the rules of the host institution, or hostel accommodation where available
Access to medical facilities available in the host institution
requirements: Complete three copies of the application form, typed or legibly handwritten in ink
Obtain endorsement from the applicant's Indian embassy or mission abroad
Foreign students in India must apply through the university they propose to work with, with embassy endorsement
Submit a six-monthly progress report by the end of June and December, signed by the supervisor, head of department and registrar
documents: Three certified copies of the university or college record
Three typed copies of a statement of not more than 500 words describing the research plan
One certified copy of the birth certificate or evidence of date of birth
Three recent passport size photographs, one stapled to each form
Abstract of the proposed plan of research of about 500 words in triplicate
Embassy or mission endorsement of the application
existing.english_requirement: The official application form and guidelines are published in English by UGC.
application_method: Apply through the Indian embassy or Indian mission in the applicant's country, which screens locally and forwards to UGC
Foreign nationals already studying in India may apply through the university they propose to work with, endorsed by the embassy
existing.selection_notes: Applications go to a short-listing and screening committee, then to a selection committee. UGC conveys provisional intimation only; the formal award letter is issued after political clearance from the Ministry of Home Affairs and the Ministry of External Affairs. UGC reserves the right to withdraw or cancel an award, and the entire fellowship is refunded if the award is discontinued before two years. No TA/DA is provided for interviews.
existing.best_fit: Master's-level holders from developing countries in Asia, Africa and Latin America seeking an M.Phil or PhD in India, and doctorate holders seeking postdoctoral research.
existing.notes: Not open to Indian citizens. It is a stipend-based research award, so no tuition is claimed as covered even though the host university charges fees. Current monetary rates could not be re-confirmed from a live UGC HTML page; the figures above are the rates published in UGC's own scheme document and may have been revised upward.
existing.duration: Four years, non-extendable, for both JRF and RA
existing.application_period: Annual, circulated through Indian embassies and Indian missions abroad. Foreign students already in India apply through the university they propose to work with.
existing.deadline_display: No fixed calendar deadline is published. The official guidelines state that "The applications are invited through circulation to Indian embassies/Indian missions abroad", so the timing is set by each mission's local call.
existing.program_type: Research fellowship for foreign nationals at Indian universities
